title: Green Code or Costly Code? Evaluating the Energy Costs of Iterative LLM-Based Code Optimizations
abstract: arXiv:2610.32891v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: Large Language Models (LLMs) are increasingly used to optimize code for performance. This practice often assumes that improvements in execution speed naturally translate into overall lower energy consumption. We challenge this assumption empirically by measuring whether performance-optimized code produced by LLM self-refinement pipelines is also energy-efficient relative to canonical human reference solutions, and whether the energy cost of the optimization process can be offset by subsequent execution-time savings. We evaluate 11 open-source models across four decoding configurations on all 1,000 problems of EffiBench, a state-of-the-art performance benchmark, while collecting per-process, hardware-level energy measurements throughout. Inference energy spans 0.79 to 8.68 MJ across model-variant pairs, which is roughly equivalent to the energy of 250 to 2800 GPT-4.1 queries. translated_title: 绿色代码还是昂贵代码？评估基于大语言模型的迭代式代码优化的能源成本
translated_abstract: 大语言模型（LLM）正被越来越多地用于优化代码性能。这种做法通常假设执行速度的提升会自然转化为更低的总体能耗。我们通过实证研究对这一假设提出质疑：我们测量了由LLM自我改进流水线生成的性能优化代码，相对于标准的人类参考解决方案是否也具有能效优势，以及优化过程本身的能源成本能否被后续的执行时间节省所抵消。我们在EffiBench（一个最先进的性能基准）的全部1,000个问题上，评估了11个开源模型在四种解码配置下的表现，并全程收集了逐进程的硬件级能耗测量数据。推理能耗在不同模型与配置组合之间跨越0.79至8.68兆焦耳（MJ），大致相当于250至2,800次GPT-4.1查询的能耗。限制最大输出token数量具有最大的……
tldr: 该研究通过对11个开源模型在EffiBench全部1000个问题上的硬件级能耗实测，挑战了“代码跑得更快就一定更省电”的假设，发现LLM迭代优化代码的推理能耗（0.79–8.68 MJ，相当于250–2800次GPT-4.1查询）未必能被后续执行时间的节省所抵消。
en_tdlr: Through hardware-level energy measurements of 11 open-source LLMs across all 1,000 EffiBench problems, this study empirically challenges the assumption that faster code means greener code, showing that the inference energy costs of LLM-based code optimization pipelines (0.79–8.68 MJ, equivalent to 250–2,800 GPT-4.1 queries) may not be offset by subsequent execution-time savings.
